name: The School Store
description: A 90-minute, 4-round basic Express simulation on running a student-run school store for a semester, for Career and Technical Education in marketing, retail merchandising, entrepreneurship and accounting, school-based enterprises of career and technical student organizations and introductory retail management. The fictional Cedar Ridge High School student business club in Lawrenceville, Georgia, runs The Talon Shop, a school store selling snacks, drinks and spirit wear, through the spring semester 2027 (11 January to 7 May) in four four-week periods. Round by round you set the price list and the spring spirit-wear buy, the snack assortment and the cash routine, the answer to an inventory count that shows shrink and the spring reorder, and the last four weeks and the end-of-semester report. Each period is scored on profit, gross margin, shrink and cash losses, students served a day and a controls-and-trust index; selling snacks that do not meet the federal Smart Snacks standards during the school day, or making the cash count sheet match the register, caps the score. English with Spanish.
view:
The School Store

One semester behind the counter of a student-run store: price it from cost, buy from the sales record, stock what sells and complies, count the cash every day, stop the shrink you can measure, and close the books honestly.

The Talon Shop · Cedar Ridge High School · Lawrenceville, Georgia · spring 2027 You are Jada Marchbanks, 17, a junior and this semester's student manager of The Talon Shop, the student business club's school store: a converted classroom by the cafeteria, open before school and through both lunches, 12 volunteers in shifts of two. It sells snacks and drinks (about $0.90 a unit from Hollins Snack Supply; about 260 a day at last year's prices) and spirit wear ($11 a piece from Ridgeback Apparel Co.; students would buy about 70, 80, 90 and 120 pieces in the four periods, if the store has their sizes). About 70% of sales are cash; fixed costs are $110 a period. The store's usual way: vending-machine prices ($1.50 a snack, $25 a shirt), last year's 400-piece order repeated (30% in sizes and old designs nobody buys), the same 24 snacks, the cash box counted on Fridays, and shrink of about 4% of sales left alone. A semester like that sells $26,742, earns $8,534, serves about 134 students a day, writes down 120 unsold pieces and ends with the controls-and-trust index at 37. Each round is scored on its four-week period: profit, gross margin, shrink and cash losses, students served a day, and controls and trust.

Round 1 — Monday 11 January 2027: the prices and the spirit-wear buy

The first day of the spring semester. Ms. Kimbrough, your student business club advisor, hands you the keys and last year's binder: no price list, no sales record by item, a stockroom full of medium hoodies with last year's logo. Dr. Strickland, the assistant principal, wants a written plan — prices and the spring spirit-wear order — on his desk by Friday. Troy Mattingly of Ridgeback Apparel offers a 600-piece bundle at $9.50 a piece; a volunteer says the store is "a captive market" and should charge $2.25 a snack and $30 a shirt.

Deliverable: the price list and the spring buy. This round is scored on 11 January–5 February.

Round 2 — Monday 8 February 2027: the snack assortment and the cash

The first period's numbers are in. Carla Thibodeaux, the district's school-nutrition director, has sent every school its Smart Snacks reminder; the volunteers say students keep asking for energy drinks and candy bars at lunch. The cash box was $31 short last Friday and nobody knows which day.

Deliverable: the snack assortment and the cash routine. This round is scored on 8 February–5 March.

Round 3 — Monday 8 March 2027: the shrink and the reorder

The first full count of the semester, taken on Friday 5 March, shows the shelves short of the records by about 4% of sales: snacks walking out at the lunch rush, "freebies" for friends, damaged stock never logged. The sizes students want — small and large — are sold out, and spring sports and prom season are coming.

Deliverable: the answer to the count and the spring reorder. This round is scored on 8 March–2 April.

Round 4 — Monday 12 April 2027: the last four weeks and the close

Four weeks to the store's last day, Friday 7 May. The seniors want a class shirt; the stockroom still holds the pieces nobody bought. Ms. Kimbrough needs the end-of-semester report — inventory, cash and profit — for the chapter and for Dr. Strickland by Friday 14 May.

Deliverable: the last four weeks and the end-of-semester report. This round is scored on 12 April–7 May.

summary.en: As Jada Marchbanks, you run The Talon Shop, the student store of Cedar Ridge High School in Lawrenceville, Georgia, for the spring 2027 semester: you set prices and the spirit-wear buy, manage snacks and cash, and respond when an inventory count shows shrink.
summary.es: Como Jada Marchbanks, llevas The Talon Shop, la tienda de los estudiantes del Cedar Ridge High School en Lawrenceville, Georgia, durante el semestre de primavera de 2027: fijas precios y la compra de ropa del instituto, gestionas aperitivos y caja y respondes cuando un recuento revela mermas.

text.en: Design a price list with a markup that covers waste, shrink and fixed costs at a level students still choose, and plan the apparel buy and snack assortment from the sales record by item
text.es: Diseñar una lista de precios con un margen sobre coste que cubra mermas, hurtos y costes fijos a un nivel que los alumnos sigan eligiendo, y planificar la compra de ropa y el surtido de snacks a partir del registro de ventas por artículo

text.en: Measure shrink with counts, reduce it with simple controls, size a reorder to what sold out and weigh consignment against owning the stock
text.es: Medir las pérdidas de inventario con recuentos, reducirlas con controles sencillos, dimensionar un nuevo pedido según lo que se agotó y comparar el depósito en consignación con la compra del inventario

text.en: Reconcile cash daily with two people, comparing the count with the point-of-sale report, recording any over or short and depositing the same day, never forcing a count to match
text.es: Cuadrar la caja cada día entre dos personas, comparando el recuento con el informe del punto de venta, registrando el sobrante o faltante y depositando el mismo día, sin forzar nunca que el recuento cuadre

text.en: Apply the Smart Snacks standards to the store's assortment and keep the store inside the school's rules for its money and its time
text.es: Aplicar las normas Smart Snacks al surtido de la tienda y mantenerla dentro de las reglas del centro sobre su dinero y su horario

text.en: Recommend an end-of-season sell-through with pre-orders and clearance rather than deep discounts, and report profit rather than sales after a physical inventory valued at cost
text.es: Recomendar un cierre de temporada con reservas y liquidación en lugar de grandes descuentos, e informar del beneficio y no de las ventas tras un inventario físico valorado al coste
